concept.name: Wyckoff Phase B
concept.definition: The second phase of a Wyckoff trading range, in which institutions build a 'cause' for the next trend by accumulating (or distributing) inventory over an extended period, sometimes a year or more. Its characteristic back-and-forth price action reflects large operators buying low and checking rallies (or the reverse in distribution).
concept.intuition: The long, boring middle of the range where the big players quietly load or unload the truck, one oscillation at a time.
concept.mechanics: Within the Phase A boundaries, price swings repeatedly between support and resistance. Early swings are wide with high volume; as professionals absorb supply (accumulation) or demand (distribution), volume on counter-swings diminishes. Multiple secondary tests and upthrust-type actions occur, and the aggregate horizontal extent of Phase B largely determines the point-and-figure count and hence the price objective.
concept.failure_modes: Phase B can extend far longer than expected, exhausting the analyst's patience and capital; the range can also resolve opposite to the presumed accumulation or distribution reading.
concept.misconceptions: Phase B is not dead time to be traded aggressively in both directions; its function is cause-building, and the balance of volume on rallies versus reactions — not the day-to-day noise — carries the analytical information.
concept.example: For nine months a stock oscillates between 90 and 102; volume on declines shrinks steadily while rallies hold their gains, and the analyst reads Phase B accumulation and measures a 20-column P&F count.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
citations.section: Accumulation: Wyckoff Phases (Phase B); Distribution: Wyckoff Phases (Phase B)
